title: Heterogeneous prefix merging and fragment slab allocation for cross-request dedupe
creator: Alicia Gomez
description:
Problem: Prefix/ prompt fragments across independent requests create redundant KV entries that consume GPU-resident memory and increase per-token cost. Continuous batching already helps amortize compute, but KV residency and fragmentation mean we still waste memory and stall on eviction. Goal: design a runtime-level merge and slab-allocation strategy that can safely deduplicate functionally-equivalent prefix fragments across tenants and requests while preserving privacy boundaries and latency SLOs.

Proposal summary: Implement a heterogeneous prefix merging layer (HPM) and a fragment slab allocator (FSA). HPM groups candidate prefixes using a lightweight similarity signature (token-histogram plus locality-sensitive hash) and a conservative Jaccard threshold to identify functionally equivalent fragments. FSA manages variable-length GPU slabs (micro, standard, large) and places merged fragments into size-appropriate slabs that are coalesced per-GPU. Key properties: deterministic merge decisions, versioned prefix ledger for safe invalidation, tenant-aware residency credits, and a shadow warmup path to avoid increased cold misses.

Why different from prior work: Instead of global content-addressing or bloom-heavy indexes, this design combines histogram-based similarity with targeted LSH clustering and slab binning. The slab allocator purposefully groups heterogeneous-length fragments to reduce fragmentation from variable template slots (e.g., system prompt + user prompt + dynamic slot). The approach targets scenarios where exact byte equality is rare but semantic token overlap is high (templated prompts, reused system messages).

Trade-offs and constraints: Conservative thresholds avoid semantic collisions but reduce dedupe rate; LSH adds CPU cost for signature computation (microbenchmarked at ~0.6ms/prefix); larger slabs reduce metadata overhead but risk pinning more memory for evicted fragments. We will tune slab sizes per-cluster with an autoscaler heuristic. Privacy: No cross-tenant merges by default; tenant-aware merge can be enabled for customers who opt in via configuration. All merges are recorded in the prefix ledger for auditability and rollback.

Key components and responsibilities:
- Signature generator: tokenized histogram + 64-bit LSH fingerprint. Runs in the request preprocessor and emits candidate merge keys.
- Merge coordinator: determines if two fragments should coalesce (Jaccard over histogram + LSH bucket check). Stores canonical fragment pointer in prefix ledger.
- Fragment Slab Allocator (FSA): allocates GPU slabs (micro=8KB, standard=64KB, large=256KB). Packs multiple fragments into slabs; maintains slab occupancy and eviction hint table.
- Residency credits: per-request credits that prefer reusing slabs already resident on target GPU to reduce cross-GPU transfer.
- Shadow warmup path: when a merged fragment is first introduced, we populate a nonblocking shadow cache to warm GPU residency without blocking serving path.

Metrics we will track: dedupe_rate, dedupe_memory_savings, p95_latency_regressions, p99_tail_increase, eviction_writebacks, LSH_false_positive_rate, merge_conflict_count, tenant_merge_opt_in_rate. Targets: 30% reduction in GPU KV memory for templated workloads, <10ms added p95 latency, <2% increase in p99 tail.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests validating merge correctness and rollback for versioned prefix ledger
Benchmarks show >=20% GPU KV memory reduction on templated prompt workload and >=10% on mixed workloads
No customer-facing latency regression: p95 generation latency increase <=10ms across synthetic and production traces
Shadow warmup path validated with metrics proving warmup reduces cold miss penalty by >=40%
Audit logs in prefix ledger record merge events and allow full reversal of merged pointers
comments: 2025-02-12 — Initial design review with SER runtime: agreed on LSH+histogram signatures instead of full-content hash; concerns about CPU overhead noted (A. Gomez)
2025-02-18 — Prototype SIG: implemented LSH signer and measured ~0.6ms/signature on 8-core x86; acceptable for P95 batching loads (M. Patel)
2025-02-24 — Benchmarks in staging: templated-chat workload + continuous batching saw 28% KV memory reduction with conservative thresholds; tuned slab sizes to micro/standard/large (PR opened)

2025-02-27 — PR feedback from infra-review: add versioned ledger and audit events; ensure no cross-tenant merges by default; added config flags and unit tests (code review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6128)
2025-03-01 — Observability plan: add 'merge_event' tracing span, slab occupancy gauge, and eviction hint histogram. Console dashboard mockup linked in design doc.
2025-03-03 — Blocker discovered: on GPUs with high slab churn, slab compaction adds transient latency spikes. Mitigation in plan to rate-limit compaction during high latency windows.
testing_plan: Unit tests: signature collisions, ledger versioning, slab boundary cases
Integration tests: end-to-end request flow with continuous batching enabled; assert no token corruption and correct generation outputs
Performance tests: run templated and mixed workloads with realistic concurrency and measure memory, latency, and eviction metrics
Chaos test: simulate abrupt GPU evictions and verify ledger-based rollback and fragment recovery
APM traces validation: ensure merge_event spans are present and correlated with request traces
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout: start with opt-in customers in staging cluster
Canary: enable for 5% of production traffic with tenant-merge disabled (only intra-tenant merges allowed)
Observe for 72 hours metrics and error budgets; promote to 25% if targets met; expand to 100% with tenant opt-in configuration
Backout plan: feature flag off -> ledger rollbacks to rehydrate original fragments if needed
Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and weekly dashboard checks
mitigation: If Jaccard false positives occur: raise threshold and revert recent merges via versioned ledger
If slab compaction causes tail latency: disable compaction during high-p90/p95 windows and rely on gradual eviction
If LSH CPU cost is high: sample prefixes for signature computation under load or offload signing to a separate worker pool
If cross-tenant privacy concerns arise: enforce strict tenant isolation and require explicit opt-in per customer
